subject.title: WhatsApp inter_session delivery requests can be wrongly suppressed as REPLY_SKIP / ANNOUNCE_SKIP / NO_REPLY

question: Should the WhatsApp explicit-delivery symptom be fixed by narrowing and landing the current requester-return-path PR, or by waiting for a broader structured `sessions_send` delivery-intent contract?
rationale: The remaining work changes model-facing A2A delivery semantics and overlaps an open structured handoff issue, so automation should not choose the permanent protocol/prompt direction alone.

options.title: Repair and land the narrow PR
options.body: Use the open requester-return-path PR as the concrete fix, preserving prompt-cache guardrails and adding the WhatsApp/source-reply regression proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Fold into structured handoff work
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader structured handoff contract explicitly covers delivery intent, skip/no-reply outcomes, and channel/thread inheritance.

options.body: Keep current code unchanged until maintainers have fresh live WhatsApp proof that distinguishes this symptom from legitimate `NO_REPLY` suppression.
